edges.mechanism: Possible additive antiplatelet/anticoagulant effect; curcumin inhibits CYP2C9 in vitro; INR rise reported with fluindione plus turmeric.
edges.evidence: Case report, bleeding-risk review, LactMed; rat PK change without PD change; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Turmeric has in vitro antiplatelet activity and LactMed notes possible increased bleeding with antiplatelet drugs; additive bleeding risk.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic/in vitro plus reference monograph; no controlled clinical study

edges.mechanism: CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition by curcuminoids may raise tacrolimus levels; one case of nephrotoxicity (trough 29.9 ng/mL) with high dietary turmeric, but a 10 g/day 4-day challenge in another patient showed no change.
edges.evidence: Two case reports and a review; conflicting; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Curcumin inhibits intestinal BCRP, raising sulfasalazine AUC 3.2-fold at therapeutic doses in humans; rosuvastatin exposure also raised in monkeys.
edges.evidence: Human PK study (n=8) plus primate study

edges.mechanism: Curcumin (1200 mg tid) lowered endoxifen AUC by 7.7%, and by 12.4% with piperine, possibly below efficacy threshold, more in CYP2D6 extensive metabolizers.
edges.evidence: Clinical PK study in breast cancer patients; review of natural product-cancer drug interactions

edges.mechanism: Curcumin altered talinolol exposure in opposite directions (AUC down with 300 mg/d, up 67-81% with 1000 mg/d, ABCB1-genotype dependent).
edges.evidence: Two small human PK studies; inconsistent

edges.mechanism: Piperine inhibits CYP3A4 and glucuronidation, raising carbamazepine Cmax 68.7%, and propranolol/theophylline exposure.
edges.evidence: Human PK studies of piperine 20 mg/d

edges.mechanism: Curcumin/turmeric lowers FBG about 10 mg/dL and HbA1c 0.32%; added glucose lowering with glyburide without hypoglycemia.
edges.evidence: MA of 34 RCTs; small open-label interaction study

edges.mechanism: Metformin plus nano-curcumin improved lipid, glucose and hormonal markers more than either alone in PCOS.
edges.evidence: Factorial RCT (n=200)

edges.mechanism: Duplicated curcuminoid exposure; liver injury clusters with high-dose, high-bioavailability curcuminoid products.
edges.evidence: Phytovigilance series and DILIN case series

edges.mechanism: Contains curcumin plus ginger: duplicated curcuminoid exposure and additive antiplatelet potential.
edges.evidence: Inferred from component evidence

edges.mechanism: Piperine increases curcumin bioavailability by 2000% and is frequently present in turmeric products implicated in liver injury.
edges.evidence: Human PK study; DILIN series; case reports

edges.mechanism: Curcumin chelates ferric iron; iron-deficiency anemia reported on high-dose turmeric despite iron supplementation, though meal-level turmeric did not inhibit non-heme iron absorption.
edges.evidence: Single case report; stable-isotope study negative; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Garlic strongly associated with surgical bleeding; turmeric and garlic both show antiplatelet activity; additive bleeding risk plausible.
edges.evidence: Narrative reviews

edges.evidence: Narrative reviews; tacrolimus case challenge

edges.evidence: DILIN case series (n=10) plus case report

edges.evidence: Crossover study (n=11), product analysis, case report
